about: House recipes, batch 04 (slice B): written by Claude in a Max-plan session, original, ai-draft. Nutrition is a per-serve estimate kept as data only.

recipes.title: Pizza Scrolls with Ham and Mozzarella
recipes.summary: No-yeast scone dough rolled up with tomato paste, ham and melted mozzarella, a lunchbox favourite.
steps: Heat the oven to 200°C fan (220°C conventional) and line a tray with baking paper. Rub the butter into the flour until it looks like breadcrumbs, then stir in the milk to make a soft dough.
Roll the dough on a floured bench into a 25 x 40cm rectangle. Spread with the tomato paste and scatter with the ham, three-quarters of the mozzarella and the oregano.
Roll up from the long side, trim the ends and cut into 12 even pieces. Place cut side up on the tray and top with the remaining cheese.
Bake for 18 minutes, until golden and the cheese is bubbling. Cool for 5 minutes before serving.
notes: Snack. Per serving: 1 scroll. Keeps 3 days in the fridge; freeze for up to 2 months.
Food safety: keep the ham refrigerated until you assemble the scrolls, bake until hot throughout, and refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours.

recipes.title: Chickpea and Mushroom Party Rolls
recipes.summary: Flaky pastry rolls filled with a savoury chickpea, mushroom and smoked paprika mix.
steps: Heat the oven to 200°C fan (220°C conventional) and line a tray with baking paper. Fry the onion and mushrooms in the olive oil for 8 minutes until the liquid has evaporated and they turn golden, then stir in the paprika and soy sauce and cool.
Roughly mash the chickpeas with a fork, then mix with the cooled mushrooms and breadcrumbs.
Cut each pastry sheet in half to make 4 strips. Spoon the filling down the centre of each strip, brush one edge with soy milk and roll to enclose with the seam underneath.
Cut each roll into 4, place seam side down on the tray, brush with soy milk and bake for 25 minutes, until deep golden and puffed.
notes: Snack. Per serving: 2 rolls. Check the pastry label for dairy and egg if serving vegans. Keeps 3 days in the fridge; reheat at 180°C fan for 8 minutes.

recipes.title: Pork and Apple Sausage Rolls
recipes.summary: Juicy pork and apple filling in golden puff pastry with a hint of wholegrain mustard.

items: 1 egg yolk, mixed with 1 tbsp water, for glazing

steps: Heat the oven to 200°C fan (220°C conventional) and line a tray with baking paper. Mix the pork, apple, onion, breadcrumbs, egg and mustard with your hands until well combined.
Cut each pastry sheet in half. Shape the filling into 4 logs, lay one along each strip, brush the edge with glaze and roll to enclose with the seam underneath.
Cut each roll into 4, place seam side down on the tray and brush with glaze.
Bake for 30 minutes, until deep golden and the pork reaches at least 75°C in the centre.
notes: Snack. Per serving: 2 rolls. Keeps 3 days in the fridge; reheat until steaming hot.
Food safety: mince must reach at least 75°C in the centre. Wash your hands, board and bench after handling raw pork and egg, and refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours.

recipes.title: Soft Pretzels with Mustard
recipes.summary: Chewy, deep-brown pretzels dipped in a bicarbonate bath, sprinkled with salt and served with mustard.

items: 1 egg yolk, mixed with 1 tbsp water

steps: Mix the flour, yeast, sugar and salt, then add the warm water and oil and knead for 8 minutes until smooth and elastic. Cover and prove for 1 hour until doubled.
Heat the oven to 220°C fan (240°C conventional) and line two trays. Divide the dough into 8, roll each into a 50cm rope and twist into a pretzel shape.
Bring the water and bicarbonate of soda to a gentle boil in a wide pan. Lower the pretzels in 2 at a time and simmer for 30 seconds each side until puffed, then lift out and drain.
Brush with the egg wash, sprinkle with coarse salt and bake for 14 minutes, until deep mahogany brown. Serve warm with mustard.
notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 1 pretzel with 1/2 tbsp mustard. Plus 1 hour proving. Best the day they are made.
Food safety: wash your hands and the bench after handling raw egg yolk. The bicarbonate bath is alkaline; do not splash it into your eyes.

recipes.title: Spinach and Feta Filo Triangles
recipes.summary: Crisp buttery filo parcels filled with spinach, feta and dill.

items: 250g frozen spinach, thawed and squeezed dry

steps: Heat the oven to 180°C fan (200°C conventional) and line a tray. Mix the spinach, feta, egg, dill and nutmeg.
Lay 1 sheet of filo on the bench, keeping the rest covered with a damp tea towel. Brush with butter, cut lengthwise into 2 strips, and place 1 tbsp filling at the end of each strip.
Fold the corner over the filling to form a triangle and keep folding along the strip to the end. Repeat with the remaining sheets to make 16 triangles.
Place seam side down on the tray, brush with butter and bake for 20 minutes, until deep golden and crisp.
notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 2 triangles. Keeps 2 days in the fridge; crisp up in a 160°C fan oven for 8 minutes.
Food safety: wash your hands and the bench after handling raw egg.

recipes.title: Frankfurt Muffin Bites
recipes.summary: Cheesy savoury muffins with a chunk of frankfurt in each, great hot or cold for kids.
steps: Heat the oven to 180°C fan (200°C conventional) and grease a 12-hole muffin tin. Whisk the egg, milk and butter together.
Stir in the flour, cheese and chives until just combined, then divide among the holes.
Press half a frankfurt into the centre of each muffin.
Bake for 20 minutes, until golden and a skewer comes out clean. Cool for 5 minutes.
notes: Snack. Per serving: 2 muffins. Keeps 3 days in the fridge; freeze for 2 months.
Food safety: keep the frankfurts refrigerated until use, bake until piping hot, and refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours. Wash your hands after handling raw egg.

recipes.title: Cheese and Corn Muffins
recipes.summary: Savoury muffins with sweet corn, sharp cheese and chives, mixed in one bowl.

items: 100g grated vegetarian hard cheese, cheddar style

steps: Heat the oven to 180°C fan (200°C conventional) and line a 12-hole muffin tin with paper cases. Mix the flour, three-quarters of the cheese, the corn and chives.
Whisk the eggs, milk and butter together, tip into the dry mix and fold until just combined.
Divide among the cases, scatter with the remaining cheese and bake for 22 minutes, until golden and a skewer comes out clean.
Cool in the tin for 5 minutes before lifting out.
notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 1 muffin. Keeps 3 days airtight; freezes for 2 months.
Food safety: wash your hands and the bench after handling raw egg.

recipes.title: Pumpkin and Feta Muffins
recipes.summary: Moist savoury muffins with grated pumpkin, creamy feta and pumpkin seeds.
steps: Heat the oven to 180°C fan (200°C conventional) and line a 12-hole muffin tin with paper cases. Mix the flour, pumpkin, feta and thyme.
Whisk the eggs, milk and oil together, tip into the dry mix and fold until just combined.
Divide among the cases, scatter with the pumpkin seeds and bake for 25 minutes, until golden and a skewer comes out clean.
Cool in the tin for 5 minutes before lifting out.
notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 1 muffin. Keeps 3 days in the fridge; freezes for 2 months.
Food safety: wash your hands and the bench after handling raw egg.

recipes.title: Cheddar Oat Crackers
recipes.summary: Crisp, nutty crackers with oats and sharp cheese, rolled thin and baked.

items: 100g grated vegetarian hard cheese, cheddar style

steps: Heat the oven to 170°C fan (190°C conventional) and line two trays. Blitz the oats in a food processor for 20 seconds until coarse, then add the flour, cheese, butter and salt and pulse until crumbly.
Add the water and pulse until the dough just comes together.
Roll the dough 2mm thick between two sheets of baking paper and cut into 30 squares, about 4cm. Place on the trays.
Bake for 15 minutes, until golden at the edges and crisp. Cool on the tray, as they crisp further as they cool.
notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 5 crackers. Keeps 1 week airtight.

recipes.title: Smoky Roasted Paprika Chickpeas
recipes.summary: Crunchy oven-roasted chickpeas with smoked paprika and garlic, a high-fibre snack.

items: 2 x 400g tins chickpeas, drained and rinsed

steps: Heat the oven to 200°C fan (220°C conventional). Dry the chickpeas very well on a clean tea towel for 3 minutes, removing any loose skins.
Toss with the olive oil on a lined tray and roast for 20 minutes, until starting to colour.
Shake the tray, add the paprika, garlic powder and salt and toss to coat.
Roast for a further 10 minutes until deep golden and crunchy. Cool for 10 minutes, as they crisp up further.
notes: Snack. Vegan, gluten-free. Per serving: about 1/2 cup (120g). Best the day they are made; keeps 2 days uncovered, then loses crunch.

recipes.title: Super Seed Crackers
recipes.summary: Thin, crisp gluten-free crackers made from sunflower, pumpkin and sesame seeds.
steps: Heat the oven to 150°C fan (170°C conventional) and line a large tray with baking paper. Whisk the cornflour with 50ml cold water, pour in the boiling water and stir for 1 minute until clear and thick.
Mix in the seeds, oats and salt and rest for 5 minutes until the gel is absorbed.
Spread very thinly, about 3mm, over the tray and score into 24 pieces.
Bake for 45 minutes, until dry, golden and crisp, turning the tray halfway. Cool on the tray, then snap apart.
notes: Snack. Vegan. Per serving: 4 crackers. Keeps 2 weeks airtight. Use certified gluten-free oats if required.

recipes.title: Crispy Baked Apple Chips
recipes.summary: Paper-thin apple slices dried in a low oven until crisp, with a dusting of cinnamon.
steps: Heat the oven to 100°C fan (120°C conventional) and line two trays with baking paper. Slice the apples 2mm thick, ideally with a mandoline, and toss in the lemon juice.
Lay the slices in a single layer and dust with cinnamon.
Bake for 90 minutes, flipping once at 45 minutes, until dry at the edges and just starting to crisp.
Turn off the oven and leave in for 15 minutes more, until crisp. They crisp more as they cool.
notes: Snack. Vegan, gluten-free. Per serving: about a quarter of the batch. Keeps 5 days airtight.

recipes.title: Mango Fruit Leather
recipes.summary: Chewy sheets of baked mango puree with a squeeze of lemon, no added sugar beyond a touch of honey.
steps: Heat the oven to 80°C fan (100°C conventional) and line a tray with baking paper. Blend the mango, lemon juice and honey for 1 minute until completely smooth.
Spread the puree 3mm thick across the tray, leaving a 2cm border.
Bake for 3 hours, until no longer sticky in the centre when touched.
Cool on the tray, peel off with the paper and cut into 8 strips.
notes: Snack. Vegetarian, not vegan (honey). Per serving: 1 strip. Keeps 2 weeks in the fridge, rolled in baking paper.

recipes.title: Berry Yoghurt Bark
recipes.summary: Frozen Greek yoghurt spread thin with berries, honey and pistachios, snapped into shards.
steps: Line a tray with baking paper. Stir the yoghurt and honey together until smooth and spread 1cm thick over the paper.
Scatter with the berries and pistachios and press them in lightly.
Freeze for 3 hours, until completely solid.
Break into 12 pieces and serve straight from the freezer.
notes: Snack. Vegetarian, not vegan (honey and dairy). Contains tree nuts. Per serving: 2 pieces. Plus 3 hours freezing. Keeps 1 month in the freezer.

recipes.title: Sesame Kale Chips
recipes.summary: Light, crackly baked kale leaves with sesame oil and sesame seeds.

items: 200g kale, stems removed and torn into bite-size pieces

steps: Heat the oven to 150°C fan (170°C conventional) and line two trays with baking paper. Wash the kale and dry it completely, as any water will make it soggy.
Toss with both oils and the salt, rubbing it in with your hands.
Spread in a single layer on the trays and sprinkle with the sesame seeds.
Bake for 15 minutes, turning the trays halfway, until crisp but still green; remove any that brown early.
notes: Snack. Vegan, gluten-free. Per serving: half the batch. Best eaten the same day.

recipes.title: Garden Summer Rolls with Peanut Soy Dip
recipes.summary: Fresh, chewy rice paper rolls packed with crunchy vegetables, vermicelli and herbs, with a quick peanut dipping sauce.

items: 1 Lebanese cucumber (100g), cut into thin sticks

steps: Soak the vermicelli in boiling water for 5 minutes until soft, then drain and rinse under cold water.
Whisk the peanut butter, soy sauce, lime juice and warm water until smooth for the dip.
Dip 1 rice paper sheet in warm water for 10 seconds until just pliable, lay it flat and pile on some vermicelli, carrot, cucumber, mint and lettuce.
Fold in the sides, roll up tightly and place on a plate under a damp cloth. Repeat to make 12 rolls and serve with the dip.
notes: Snack. Vegan. Contains peanuts. Per serving: 3 rolls with dip. Best eaten within 2 hours.

recipes.title: Baked Kumara Fries with Lime Yoghurt Dip
recipes.summary: Crisp-edged sweet potato fries with smoked paprika and a cooling lime and chive dip.
steps: Heat the oven to 200°C fan (220°C conventional) and line two trays with baking paper. Toss the sweet potato with the oil, paprika and salt, spread in a single layer with space between the sticks.
Bake for 35 minutes, turning once at 20 minutes, until the edges are crisp and golden and the centres are tender.
Mix the yoghurt, lime juice and chives for the dip.
Serve the fries hot with the dip.
notes: Snack. Vegetarian, gluten-free. Per serving: a quarter of the fries with dip. Best eaten straight away.

recipes.title: Peanut Choc Energy Balls
recipes.summary: No-bake oat balls with peanut butter, cocoa and honey, ready to roll in 15 minutes.
steps: Mix the oats, peanut butter, honey and cocoa in a bowl until a sticky dough forms, adding 1 tbsp water if it is crumbly.
Chill the mixture for 20 minutes until firm enough to roll.
Roll level tablespoons into 16 balls, about 25g each.
Roll in the coconut and store in the fridge.
notes: Snack. Vegetarian, not vegan (honey). Contains peanuts. Per serving: 2 balls. Plus 20 minutes chilling. Keeps 1 week in the fridge.

recipes.title: Pumpkin Seed and Honey Clusters
recipes.summary: Crunchy baked oat clusters with pepitas, honey and cinnamon, ideal over yoghurt or by the handful.
steps: Heat the oven to 150°C fan (170°C conventional) and line a tray with baking paper. Warm the honey and oil together for 1 minute until runny and stir in the cinnamon.
Mix with the oats and pumpkin seeds until well coated.
Press firmly into a flat layer on the tray and bake for 25 minutes, until golden brown, without stirring.
Cool completely, then break into clusters and mix in the sultanas.
notes: Snack. Vegetarian, not vegan (honey). Per serving: about 1/2 cup. Keeps 2 weeks airtight.

recipes.title: Cucumber Hummus Bites
recipes.summary: Cool cucumber rounds topped with creamy home-made hummus and a dusting of paprika.
steps: Blend the chickpeas, tahini, lemon juice, garlic, olive oil and water for 2 minutes until smooth and creamy, adding a little more water if it is too thick.
Season with a pinch of salt.
Spoon or pipe about 1 tbsp of the hummus onto each cucumber round.
Dust with paprika and serve straight away.
notes: Snack. Vegan, gluten-free. Contains sesame. Per serving: 6 bites. Keeps 1 day in the fridge.

recipes.title: Mini Pizza Toasts
recipes.summary: Crisp sourdough squares with tomato, mozzarella and capsicum, grilled until bubbling.
steps: Heat the oven to 200°C fan (220°C conventional) and line a tray. Lay the bread slices on the tray and toast for 3 minutes until just firm.
Spread each slice with the tomato paste and top with the capsicum, oregano and mozzarella.
Bake for 7 minutes, until the cheese is melted and golden.
Cut each slice into quarters and serve warm.
notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 1 slice (4 pieces). Best eaten warm.

recipes.title: Apple and Peanut Butter Sandwiches
recipes.summary: Crisp apple rings sandwiched with peanut butter and sunflower seeds, no cooking needed.
steps: Slice the apples into 8 rounds, about 8mm thick, and brush with the lemon juice to stop them browning.
Spread peanut butter on 4 of the rounds until it reaches the edges.
Scatter with the sunflower seeds and top with the remaining rounds, pressing lightly.
Cut each sandwich in half and serve straight away.
notes: Snack. Vegan, gluten-free. Contains peanuts. Per serving: 1 sandwich. Eat within 2 hours.

recipes.title: Rainbow Fruit Skewers with Honey Yoghurt
recipes.summary: Colourful skewers of watermelon, pineapple, mango and orange with a honey yoghurt dip for kids' parties.
steps: Thread the fruit onto 8 short skewers until each is full, in rainbow order: watermelon, orange, mango, pineapple. Trim any sharp ends or use paddle-pop sticks for young children.
Stir the honey into the yoghurt.
Serve the skewers with the dip on the side.
Chill under cling film until serving and eat within 2 hours.
notes: Snack. Vegetarian, gluten-free. Per serving: 2 skewers with dip. Use blunt skewers for children under 5, and cut fruit small to avoid choking.

recipes.title: Ham and Cheese Pinwheels
recipes.summary: Flaky puff pastry rolled with ham, cheese and mustard, sliced into party pinwheels.

items: 100g grated vegetarian hard cheese, cheddar style

steps: Heat the oven to 200°C fan (220°C conventional) and line two trays. Spread the pastry sheets with the mustard and scatter over the ham and cheese.
Roll each sheet up tightly from one side, wrap and chill for 15 minutes until firm.
Slice each roll into 12 rounds, place cut side up on the trays and brush with the egg.
Bake for 20 minutes, until puffed and golden brown. Cool for 5 minutes.
notes: Snack. Per serving: 3 pinwheels. Plus 15 minutes chilling. Keeps 3 days in the fridge; reheat until hot.
Food safety: keep the ham refrigerated until you assemble, bake until hot throughout, and refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours. Wash your hands after handling raw egg.

recipes.title: Herb and Cheese Drop Biscuits
recipes.summary: Fluffy savoury biscuits made with buttermilk, cheese and fresh herbs, with no rolling or cutting.

items: 100g grated vegetarian hard cheese, cheddar style

steps: Heat the oven to 200°C fan (220°C conventional) and line a tray with baking paper. Rub the butter into the flour until it looks like breadcrumbs.
Stir in the cheese and herbs, then add the buttermilk and mix until a rough, sticky dough forms.
Drop 12 heaped spoonfuls (about 60g each) onto the tray.
Bake for 15 minutes, until risen and golden brown. Cool for 5 minutes and serve warm.
notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 1 biscuit. Best on the day; freezes for 2 months.

recipes.title: Egg and Chive Mini Frittatas
recipes.summary: Protein-packed mini frittatas with spinach and cheese, baked in a muffin tin.
steps: Heat the oven to 160°C fan (180°C conventional) and grease a 12-hole muffin tin. Whisk the eggs, milk and salt together.
Divide the spinach, cheese and chives among the holes and pour in the egg mix.
Bake for 15 minutes, until set in the centre with no liquid egg left and lightly golden.
Cool in the tin for 3 minutes, then lift out.
notes: Snack. Vegetarian, gluten-free. Per serving: 3 frittatas. Keeps 3 days in the fridge; reheat until steaming hot.
Food safety: cook until the egg is fully set, wash your hands and the bench after handling raw egg, and refrigerate within 2 hours.
